original_question: Given an ideal digital filter, meaning a nonnegative even step function on [-pi, pi], find a rational function H(z) with poles inside the open unit disk D such that the boundary magnitude |H(e^{is})| approximates the target response chi(e^{is}).
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, read together with the notation/translation supplied by Proposition 1.2 and the first proved special case in Theorem 1.3: whether every ideal digital filter can be uniformly approximated on the unit circle by the boundary modulus of a rational function whose poles lie in the open unit disk.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main mathematical actors and the right qualitative goal: the target is an ideal digital filter on [-pi, pi]; the approximant is a rational transfer function H(z); stability is encoded by requiring poles in the open unit disk D; and the approximation is made at the boundary through |H(e^{is})|. It also correctly reflects that the paper is about approximating an ideal frequency response rather than matching it exactly.
missing_details: The paper’s main formulation is epsilon-quantified: for every ideal digital filter chi and every epsilon > 0, one asks whether there exists such a rational H.

The target chi is not just an arbitrary nonnegative even step function; in the paper it is an ideal digital filter in the characteristic-function sense, i.e. a {0,1}-valued even step function, equivalently the indicator of a symmetric finite union of arcs on the unit circle.
The ambient boundary set should be stated explicitly as the unit circle T = {e^{is} : s in [-pi, pi]}.
The approximation mode should be stated explicitly as uniform approximation on T (or the exact norm used in the paper’s formulation).
The rational function lives in C(z); the draft does not specify the ambient coefficient field.
The symmetry built into the target (evenness / conjugation symmetry) should be stated as part of the data of the problem, not left implicit.
There is no degree bound in the conjectural statement; it is a pure existence question over all rational functions with poles in D.
The paper’s nearby equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2 is not reflected in the draft.
The role of Theorem 1.3 as a proved special case near the conjecture is omitted, so the current draft does not signal the exact scope of what is open versus what is already established.
refined_question: Let chi = chi_E be an ideal digital filter, where E is a finite union of arcs of the unit circle T that is symmetric under complex conjugation, so that s -> chi(e^{is}) is an even {0,1}-valued step function on [-pi, pi]. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a rational function H in C(z), all of whose poles lie in the open unit disk D, such that the boundary magnitude of H uniformly approximates chi on T; equivalently, sup_{s in [-pi, pi]} ||H(e^{is})| - chi(e^{is})| < epsilon?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s main open approximation problem from the introduction: approximation of an ideal digital filter by the boundary modulus of a stable rational function. The nearest paper-faithful sharpening is therefore the epsilon-uniform existence question of Conjecture 1.1, with Proposition 1.2 supplying the precise surrounding notation/reformulation and Theorem 1.3 giving the nearby proved case. The main repairs needed are: making chi a characteristic-function-type ideal filter rather than an arbitrary nonnegative step function; restoring the universal quantifiers; stating the unit-circle boundary and the approximation norm explicitly; and keeping the question as a pure existence problem with no added degree or regularity hypotheses.
